skill.name: tmux-processes
skill.description: Guidance for managing long-running development processes in tmux sessions and project-scoped windows.
skill.summary: Run, monitor, restart, and isolate long-lived development processes with tmux.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and documented tmux shell examples. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, hidden scripts, network access, or malicious process-management intent was found.

remediation.issue: Command examples use placeholders that rely on agent judgment.
remediation.suggestion: State that placeholder commands must come from the user or existing project scripts before using tmux send-keys.

content.value_statement: Long-running dev servers and watchers can lose output or block agent work. This skill gives tmux patterns for starting, monitoring, restarting, and isolating those processes.
actual_capabilities: Derives tmux session names from the current project root.
Starts long-running commands in named tmux windows.
Checks existing sessions and windows before launching duplicates.
Captures pane output to inspect errors and readiness messages.
Restarts a process by sending Ctrl+C and a replacement command.
Defines isolation rules to avoid killing unrelated tmux sessions.
limitations: Requires tmux and common shell tools in the runtime environment.
Requires the agent or user to choose safe project commands.
Does not prove service health beyond captured terminal output.
Not intended for quick one-shot commands that need direct output.

use_cases.title: Launch Local Development
use_cases.description: Start a dev server in tmux and monitor output without blocking the conversation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Watchers
use_cases.description: Run test watchers, file watchers, and logs in separate project windows.

use_cases.title: Standardize Agent Operations
use_cases.description: Give coding agents predictable rules for process lifecycle and session cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Start One Process
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single long-running command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Start my development server in tmux for this project, then check recent output and tell me whether it is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Run Server and Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Use named windows for related project processes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the app server and test watcher in separate tmux windows for this project. Report each window name and current status.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Existing Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Check process state before changing anything.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this project already has a tmux session. Capture recent output from the server window and summarize any errors.

prompt_templates.title: Restart and Verify Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced lifecycle management with readiness checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Restart the server window in this project tmux session. Poll recent output for readiness, then report success or the first blocking error.

output_examples.input: Start the dev server in tmux and check if it is ready.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a project-named session, starts the server in a server window, and reports the latest readiness lines.

output_examples.input: Add a test watcher without disturbing the server.
output_examples.output: The agent checks the existing session, adds a tests window if needed, and confirms both windows remain available.

output_examples.input: Restart the server and watch for errors.
output_examples.output: The agent sends an interrupt to the server window, starts the command again, and summarizes the captured error or ready message.

best_practices: Derive the session name from the project root before starting or stopping processes.
Use named windows for each service, watcher, or log stream.
Capture pane output before deciding whether a process is ready or failing.
anti_patterns: Do not use tmux kill-server for project cleanup.
Do not create duplicate sessions before checking existing state.
Do not use tmux for short commands that need immediate stdout.

faq.question: What does this skill help manage?
faq.answer: It helps agents run long-lived development commands inside tmux sessions and named windows.

faq.question: Does it start processes automatically?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for the agent to follow when the user asks for long-running processes.

faq.question: Why use tmux instead of a normal shell command?
faq.answer: tmux keeps the process running while preserving output for later inspection.

faq.question: Can it manage multiple processes?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends one project session with separate windows for servers, tests, logs, and watchers.

faq.question: How does it avoid disrupting other work?
faq.answer: It derives project-specific session names and warns against killing unrelated sessions.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The environment needs tmux. Some examples also use git, basename, grep or rg, and standard shell tools.
